title: Hsp82: ATP binding versus hydrolysis in client maturation
objective: Distinguish nucleotide occupancy, hydrolytic chemistry, conformational coupling and nucleotide-state resetting in client maturation. Use a defined yeast Hsp82 homodimer background and client-specific function alongside loading, release and stability; do not use viability or ATPase as substitutes for maturation.
coordinate_note: All positions use S. cerevisiae S288c Hsp82 UniProt P02829 SV1. Each construct is one distinct 709-aa chain with copies:2, describing a homodimer of identical protomers (1418 aa total), not two concatenated chains. Each double mutant adds one substitution to its E33A parent. Tag-free proteins retain a free MEEVD C terminus. Domain borders are operational annotations, not proposed cleavage sites.

sources.title: The Charged Linker Modulates the Conformations and Molecular Interactions of Hsp90
sources.coverage: Europe PMC full text; inspected Introduction and NMR construct-boundary Results for NTD, charged linker and MD. Functional display partitions are operational; isolated-domain and structural definitions differ. No truncation is proposed.

regions.name: Nucleotide-binding NTD
regions.description: Operational native 1-210 nucleotide module. E33 participates in hydrolytic chemistry; D79 contacts adenine; K98 affects nucleotide interactions. The ATP lid and N-terminal dimer interface couple occupancy to conformation.

regions.name: Charged linker
regions.description: Operational native 211-272, including the N-linker segment sometimes included in NTD constructs ending at 217 or 220. Preserved in every variant.

regions.name: Client/coupling MD
regions.description: Operational native 273-529, matching an NMR MD construct. Includes E372 and R380 and contributes client/cochaperone interactions. Some structural middle-domain constructs extend to 560; these are different operational boundaries.

regions.name: C-terminal assembly region
regions.description: Operational native 530-704 includes the interdomain hinge, C-terminal dimerization machinery and flexible tail preceding MEEVD. This is a display partition, not a claim that residue 530 is a universal structural boundary; no truncation is proposed.

regions.name: MEEVD docking motif
regions.description: Native free C-terminal 705-709 MEEVD motif recruits TPR cochaperones. Kept accessible by omitting C-terminal tags.

variants.name: WT Hsp82
variants.headline: Native homodimer reference

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: UniProt P02829 sequence version 1; complete 709-aa untagged S. cerevisiae S288c protomer. The intended assembly is a homodimer of identical protomers; verify dimerization experimentally.

variants.note: Reference chosen because the binding, hydrolysis, suppressor and ADP-affinity mutations were compared in this isoform. No purification tag, coiled coil, reporter cysteine, client or cochaperone is implicit.

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: Both protomers carry the stated changes. No WT/mutant heterodimer or mixed population is encoded.

rationale.hypothesis: Does nucleotide occupancy contribute to maturation beyond client binding by an apo scaffold?

observations.finding: D79N nucleotide-binding-defective variants failed to support yeast viability, whereas E33A variants retained condition-dependent function.
observations.context: Yeast Hsp82 and other Hsp90 orthologs expressed as the sole Hsp90 in plasmid-shuffle assays. This is a cellular complementation endpoint, not a direct client-maturation measurement.

observations.finding: Human Hsp90alpha E47A failed GR ligand-binding recovery after Hsp70 inhibition, but Bag-1-assisted Hsp70 release allowed E47A to maintain GR function.
observations.context: Reconstituted human Hsp90alpha/Hsp70/HOP/p23, yeast Ydj1 and GRLBD(F602S); this distinguishes release from maintenance in that system.

rationale.comparison: Compare with WT and E33A at matched soluble dimer concentration. Measure ATP/ADP binding, client loading and client-specific activity. Retained client association with poor activity separates loading from productive maturation.
rationale.uncertainty: D79N affects nucleotide binding broadly, not ATP alone, and can also alter conformation. It is not an ADP-binding-preserved ATP-selective perturbation.
rationale.edit: Disrupt the adenine-contact site while retaining the complete dimeric scaffold.
rationale.inference: D79N provides the binding-defective baseline. Its phenotype cannot by itself distinguish ATP-specific occupancy from nucleotide-dependent structural effects.

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: Both protomers carry the stated changes. No WT/mutant heterodimer or mixed population is encoded.

rationale.hypothesis: Can ATP occupancy support client maturation when hydrolysis is below detection?

observations.finding: Purified Hsp82 E33A had no detectable ATP hydrolysis with or without Aha1, yet could support yeast viability with conditional defects.
observations.context: Purified His-tagged Hsp82 ATPase assay and separate cellular complementation experiments; assay detection limits apply.

observations.finding: Hsp82 E33A supported viability but reduced v-Src activation and GR reporter activity; the reported GR reduction was modest rather than complete.
observations.context: Hsp82 as sole Hsp90 in yeast; heterologous v-Src toxicity and GR-dependent beta-galactosidase reporter. These assays are not direct ligand-binding recovery.

observations.finding: E33A changed how ATP and nonhydrolysable analogs stabilized the closed clamp; ATP and ATP analogs were not interchangeable probes.
observations.context: Engineered Hsp82 PET reporters in vitro; results describe the tested reporter and nucleotide conditions.

observations.finding: Human Hsp90alpha E47A failed GR ligand-binding recovery after Hsp70 inhibition, but Bag-1-assisted Hsp70 release allowed E47A to maintain GR function.
observations.context: Reconstituted human Hsp90alpha/Hsp70/HOP/p23, yeast Ydj1 and GRLBD(F602S); this distinguishes release from maintenance in that system.

rationale.comparison: Compare with WT and D79N. Establish ATP binding and absence of detectable Hsp82 ATPase, then measure functional client output, loading/release and conformation under the same nucleotide regime.
rationale.uncertainty: E33A alters conformational equilibria and analog responses as well as chemistry. A defect is not proof that hydrolysis energy is the direct missing requirement; retained viability is not proof of normal client maturation.
rationale.edit: Remove the catalytic carboxylate while retaining the full-length nucleotide-binding scaffold.
rationale.inference: E33A is an established separation-of-function starting point whose client and condition dependence must be measured, not assumed.

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: Both protomers carry the stated changes. No WT/mutant heterodimer or mixed population is encoded.

rationale.hypothesis: What effect does the suppressor have when hydrolysis remains available?

observations.finding: E372K suppressed growth and cell-wall-integrity defects of E33A without restoring detectable ATP hydrolysis; GAL induction was improved but not restored to WT.
observations.context: Hsp82 E33A/E372K in yeast; CWI/GAL pathway readouts and purified Hsp82 ATPase assays. Direct GR or Ste11 catalytic rescue was not demonstrated.

observations.finding: E372K changed E33A conformational responses and restored stronger ATP-gamma-S-induced closed-clamp stabilization.
observations.context: Engineered Hsp82 PET reporters. This supports allosteric rescue, not a measured increase in nucleotide-exchange rate.

rationale.comparison: Use the complete four-way comparison WT, E33A, E372K and E33A/E372K. Quantify direct client activity and nucleotide/closure kinetics rather than a growth reporter alone.
rationale.uncertainty: E372K is not an inert background: it can change MD coupling, client/cochaperone interactions and nucleotide responses. Single-mutant behavior in the chosen client assay remains to be established.
rationale.edit: Isolate the contribution of the middle-domain suppressor without the catalytic mutation.
rationale.inference: The single mutant is required to distinguish specific rescue of E33A from a general gain or a client-specific effect.

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: Both protomers carry the stated changes. No WT/mutant heterodimer or mixed population is encoded.

rationale.hypothesis: Can allosteric rescue recover client maturation without restoring ATP hydrolysis?

observations.finding: E372K suppressed growth and cell-wall-integrity defects of E33A without restoring detectable ATP hydrolysis; GAL induction was improved but not restored to WT.
observations.context: Hsp82 E33A/E372K in yeast; CWI/GAL pathway readouts and purified Hsp82 ATPase assays. Direct GR or Ste11 catalytic rescue was not demonstrated.

observations.finding: E372K changed E33A conformational responses and restored stronger ATP-gamma-S-induced closed-clamp stabilization.
observations.context: Engineered Hsp82 PET reporters. This supports allosteric rescue, not a measured increase in nucleotide-exchange rate.

rationale.comparison: Compare with E33A and E372K as well as WT. A recovery of direct client function with verified undetectable Hsp82 ATPase and retained ATP binding would show hydrolysis is dispensable for that client/readout under those conditions. Measure exchange directly to test the proposed bypass.
rationale.uncertainty: Published rescue concerns growth, CWI and partial GAL output, not universal client maturation. Exchange acceleration is inferred from genetics; the 2025 study also supports altered closed-state coupling.
rationale.edit: Introduce the documented suppressor into the hydrolysis-defective background.
rationale.inference: This is a published genetic rescue pair used here to distinguish a chemical requirement from altered conformational progression. It is not a new proposed double mutant and does not pre-establish GR or Ste11 rescue.

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: Both protomers carry the stated changes. No WT/mutant heterodimer or mixed population is encoded.

rationale.hypothesis: How much does the nucleotide-affinity perturbation affect maturation when hydrolysis remains available?

observations.finding: K98A, previously reported to reduce ADP affinity, was tolerated alone but strongly exacerbated E33A; the double mutant barely grew.
observations.context: Yeast Hsp82 cellular epistasis; nucleotide-exchange mechanism is an interpretation that requires direct kinetic testing.

observations.finding: K98A supported viability and had near-WT ATPase activity, while altering the conformational response to ATP.
observations.context: Purified Hsp82 ATPase and PET reporter assays plus yeast complementation; affinity changes were not excluded.

rationale.comparison: Use WT, E33A, K98A and E33A/K98A as a second four-way comparison. Measure ATP and ADP affinities, occupancy/exchange and client function for each.
rationale.uncertainty: K98A is not a chemically pure ADP-off switch: it contacts nucleotide and also changes conformational response. Measure both affinities instead of assuming ATP binding is fully unchanged.
rationale.edit: Perturb nucleotide interactions without removing the catalytic glutamate.
rationale.inference: K98A supplies the matched baseline for testing whether the hydrolysis-defective background is especially dependent on access to an ADP-bound/reset state.

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: Both protomers carry the stated changes. No WT/mutant heterodimer or mixed population is encoded.

rationale.hypothesis: Does access to an ADP-bound/reset state become especially important when hydrolysis is impaired?

observations.finding: K98A, previously reported to reduce ADP affinity, was tolerated alone but strongly exacerbated E33A; the double mutant barely grew.
observations.context: Yeast Hsp82 cellular epistasis; nucleotide-exchange mechanism is an interpretation that requires direct kinetic testing.

rationale.comparison: Compare with E33A and K98A at matched intact dimer concentration and controlled ATP:ADP ratios. Test whether reduced ADP occupancy or altered exchange correlates with failure of client release and activity.
rationale.uncertainty: The published double mutant is nearly nonviable. Its client phenotype may reflect general loss of function, destabilization or conformational epistasis rather than exchange alone; purified assays avoid viability selection but still require stability checks.
rationale.edit: Combine the ADP-affinity perturbation with the hydrolysis-defective background.
rationale.inference: A disproportionate double-mutant defect is consistent with an ADP/exchange contribution but is not sufficient proof of that mechanism without direct nucleotide and conformational measurements.

chains.name: Hsp82 protomer
chains.note: Both protomers carry the stated changes. No WT/mutant heterodimer or mixed population is encoded.

rationale.hypothesis: Is ATP turnover sufficient when productive closed-state coupling is disrupted?

observations.finding: R380A retained substantial ATP turnover, approximately half the WT rate in this assay, yet failed viability and productive closed-clamp stabilization in PET.
observations.context: Purified Hsp82 ATPase, engineered PET reporter and separate yeast complementation experiments.

observations.finding: R380A altered occupancy and stability of distinct closed intermediates and reduced Sba1 engagement.
observations.context: SAXS, FRET and Sba1-binding assays with engineered/labeled yeast Hsp82 reporters. An observed closed FRET signal is not equivalent to a productive closed state.

rationale.comparison: Compare with WT and E33A. Measure residual Hsp82 ATPase, ATP binding, closed-state occupancy/dynamics, cochaperone association and client activity. Turnover with poor maturation demonstrates that turnover alone is insufficient.
rationale.uncertainty: R380A perturbs the catalytic-loop/client-coupling network and is not a permanently open or pure hydrolysis-defective mutant. Different methods resolve different closed intermediates; bulk compaction alone cannot identify a productive state.
rationale.edit: Perturb the arginine coupling ATP to middle-domain docking while preserving the dimerization region.
rationale.inference: Use as a conformational-coupling control, not as a second equivalent hydrolysis-null allele.

hypotheses.question: Is nucleotide occupancy required for productive client maturation?
hypotheses.mechanism: D79N perturbs nucleotide recognition while the intact scaffold remains available for client association.
hypotheses.measurement: ATP/ADP affinity and occupancy, soluble dimers, client loading and functional maturation versus WT and E33A.

hypotheses.question: Does maturation persist when hydrolysis is below detection?
hypotheses.mechanism: E33A retains ATP binding but strongly impairs hydrolytic chemistry and also changes conformational dynamics.
hypotheses.measurement: Hsp82-specific ATP turnover plus direct client activity, release and conformation versus WT and D79N.

hypotheses.question: Can allosteric rescue bypass a client-maturation defect without restoring hydrolysis?
hypotheses.mechanism: The documented E372K suppressor may improve productive coupling and/or nucleotide-state progression in E33A.
hypotheses.measurement: Four-way comparison of WT, E33A, E372K and E33A/E372K for client function, ATPase, affinities, nucleotide exchange and conformation.

hypotheses.question: Is ADP-state access especially important without efficient hydrolysis?
hypotheses.mechanism: K98A tests dependence on ADP occupancy/resetting in the E33A background; it may have additional structural effects.
hypotheses.measurement: Four-way comparison of WT, E33A, K98A and E33A/K98A at controlled ATP:ADP ratios, with direct affinities/exchange and client output.

hypotheses.question: Can ATP turnover be uncoupled from productive maturation?
hypotheses.mechanism: R380A changes middle-domain/ATP coupling and closed-intermediate populations despite residual ATPase.
hypotheses.measurement: ATPase, nucleotide binding, Sba1 association, conformation and client activity versus WT and E33A.

scale.higher_means: more conserved across this comparison set

method.homolog_source: UniRef50_P02829 UniProtKB cluster members retrieved 2026-11-16; Hsp90 homolog cluster, not a species-tree-validated one-to-one ortholog set
method.comparison_set: Automatically retrieved UniRef50_P02829 cluster members, not a species-tree-validated one-to-one ortholog set. Closely related cytosolic Hsp90 paralogs may be represented; interpret the profile as cluster-level evolutionary support.
method.alignment: multiple alignment by FAMSA via pyfamsa 0.7.0, projected onto reference coordinates by dropping columns where the reference is gapped; measured against MAFFT on one family it agrees closely where both score and additionally reports weak values at positions MAFFT declines, so read per-position coverage alongside the score
method.weighting: Henikoff position-based sequence weights, computed over variable columns only
method.effective_sequences_definition: Neff = sum(1/n_i), n_i counting sequences at least 80% identical to sequence i over positions where both have a residue (itself included); pairs overlapping less than 50% of the reference are not counted as similar. Reported unnormalised and divided by reference length; normalisation is not standardised in the literature, so compare only against values computed the same way. This is NOT the sum of the Henikoff weights, which is rescaled to the sequence count by construction and therefore always equals it.
method.score: Jensen-Shannon divergence against Robinson & Robinson background, scaled by column occupancy (Capra & Singh 2007)

precedent_search.scope: Completed before choosing the eight-member library. Europe PMC title/abstract searches for Hsp90/Hsp82 ATP binding, hydrolysis and nucleotide exchange dated 2024-01-01 through 2026-11-16; forward-citation searches from the 2023 and 2025 Reidy studies; primary-source web searches. Full relevant sections of 2025 ATP structural/coupling, 2024 cochaperone directionality/triage and 2026 bacterial HtpG single-molecule studies were inspected. Additional 2026 phosphorylation, ADP hydration, proteome and closed-state-binder papers were screened at abstract level. Consequences: retain E372K rescue and its single control, test K98A epistasis, measure closure and release separately, and do not generalize yeast complementation to every client or bacterial/engineered dimer context. All edits are established mechanistic variants; the client-specific comparison is a proposed experiment, not a novelty claim. Supplemental sequence/primer files were not accessible.
